claims.title: Columbus reaches Hispaniola
claims.summary: On his first voyage Christopher Columbus lands on the island the Taino call Quisqueya and claims it for Spain as La Isla Espanola, opening the European conquest of the Americas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Dominican Republic: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and Columbus's first colony to Santo Domingo, the first European city of the Americas, through Haitian unification, hard-won independence on 27 February 1844, the long shadow of Trujillo, and a modern tourism-and-services economy.", terralore.co/country/DOM/chronicle#ev-1492-columbus-reaches-hispaniola, claim TL:DOM:event:1492:columbus-reaches-hispaniola, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Santo Domingo
claims.summary: Bartholomew Columbus founds Santo Domingo on the Ozama River; refounded soon after, it becomes the oldest permanent European city in the Americas and the seat of Spanish power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Dominican Republic: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and Columbus's first colony to Santo Domingo, the first European city of the Americas, through Haitian unification, hard-won independence on 27 February 1844, the long shadow of Trujillo, and a modern tourism-and-services economy.", terralore.co/country/DOM/chronicle#ev-1496-founding-of-santo-domingo, claim TL:DOM:event:1496:founding-of-santo-domingo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First university in the Americas
claims.summary: A royal charter establishes the University of Santo Domingo, the first university in the New World, in a city already home to its first cathedral and hospital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Dominican Republic: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and Columbus's first colony to Santo Domingo, the first European city of the Americas, through Haitian unification, hard-won independence on 27 February 1844, the long shadow of Trujillo, and a modern tourism-and-services economy.", terralore.co/country/DOM/chronicle#ev-1538-first-university-in-the-americas, claim TL:DOM:event:1538:first-university-in-the-americas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Drake sacks Santo Domingo
claims.summary: The English privateer Francis Drake captures and ransoms the decayed capital, a sign of how far the once-central colony had fallen as imperial wealth moved to the mainland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Dominican Republic: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and Columbus's first colony to Santo Domingo, the first European city of the Americas, through Haitian unification, hard-won independence on 27 February 1844, the long shadow of Trujillo, and a modern tourism-and-services economy.", terralore.co/country/DOM/chronicle#ev-1586-drake-sacks-santo-domingo, claim TL:DOM:event:1586:drake-sacks-santo-domingo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Ryswick
claims.summary: Spain formally recognises French control of the western third of Hispaniola, creating the colony of Saint-Domingue beside Spanish Santo Domingo.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Dominican Republic: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and Columbus's first colony to Santo Domingo, the first European city of the Americas, through Haitian unification, hard-won independence on 27 February 1844, the long shadow of Trujillo, and a modern tourism-and-services economy.", terralore.co/country/DOM/chronicle#ev-1697-treaty-of-ryswick, claim TL:DOM:event:1697:treaty-of-ryswick, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Basel
claims.summary: By the Treaty of Basel, Spain cedes the colony of Santo Domingo to France, although the upheavals of the Haitian Revolution delay any effective handover.

claims.title: Independence of Haiti
claims.summary: After defeating France, the formerly enslaved people of Saint-Domingue proclaim Haiti, the first nation founded by a successful slave revolt, reshaping the whole island.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Dominican Republic: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and Columbus's first colony to Santo Domingo, the first European city of the Americas, through Haitian unification, hard-won independence on 27 February 1844, the long shadow of Trujillo, and a modern tourism-and-services economy.", terralore.co/country/DOM/chronicle#ev-1804-independence-of-haiti, claim TL:DOM:event:1804:independence-of-haiti, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ephemeral Independence
claims.summary: Governor Jose Nunez de Caceres declares Santo Domingo independent of Spain, hoping to join Gran Colombia; the fragile state lasts only a matter of weeks.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Dominican Republic: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and Columbus's first colony to Santo Domingo, the first European city of the Americas, through Haitian unification, hard-won independence on 27 February 1844, the long shadow of Trujillo, and a modern tourism-and-services economy.", terralore.co/country/DOM/chronicle#ev-1821-ephemeral-independence, claim TL:DOM:event:1821:ephemeral-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Haitian unification of the island
claims.summary: President Jean-Pierre Boyer occupies the east and unifies all Hispaniola under Haiti for twenty-two years, abolishing slavery but alienating much of the Dominican population.

claims.title: Founding of La Trinitaria
claims.summary: Juan Pablo Duarte founds the clandestine society La Trinitaria, organised in three-man cells, to undermine Haitian rule and build a movement for Dominican independence.

claims.title: Dominican independence from Haiti
claims.summary: The Trinitarios rise in Santo Domingo, expel the Haitian garrison, and proclaim the Dominican Republic, the date still marked as national independence day.

claims.summary: President Pedro Santana returns the republic to Spanish rule, an unprecedented step that soon provokes fierce popular resistance.

claims.summary: Rafael Trujillo, commander of the army built under the occupation, takes the presidency and establishes a personal dictatorship that lasts thirty-one years.

claims.title: The Parsley Massacre
claims.summary: Trujillo orders the army to kill Haitians and Haitian-descended people along the border; the death toll, carried out largely by machete, is estimated in the thousands to tens of thousands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Dominican Republic: From the Taino island of Quisqueya and Columbus's first colony to Santo Domingo, the first European city of the Americas, through Haitian unification, hard-won independence on 27 February 1844, the long shadow of Trujillo, and a modern tourism-and-services economy.", terralore.co/country/DOM/chronicle#ev-1937-the-parsley-massacre, claim TL:DOM:event:1937:the-parsley-massacre, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.summary: Trujillo is ambushed and gunned down near Santo Domingo by conspirators including military officers, ending the long dictatorship and opening a contested transition.

claims.summary: In the first free elections in decades, the reformist writer Juan Bosch wins the presidency, only to be overthrown by the military after seven months in 1963.

claims.summary: A Constitutionalist rising to restore Bosch sparks civil war; President Johnson sends some 22,000 U.S. troops in Operation Power Pack, the second U.S. intervention of the century.

claims.summary: In U.S.-backed elections after the intervention, the conservative Joaquin Balaguer defeats Bosch, beginning a dominance of Dominican politics that lasts three decades.
